claim: In Unbound's cost model, a national DAF sponsor running on Unbound spends about 30% less on administration than with its current workflow enhanced with AI: $245 per fund-year at the median (range $209–$288) against $351 (range $287–$480).
comparator: Approach B: the sponsor's existing workflow enhanced with AI (report 05a §1, Monte Carlo P10/P50/P90)
lever_attribution: Platform alone (B to C0): 3.4%. Redesign levers (determination reuse, fewer contacts and reconciliation breaks, outsourced complex gifts; C0 to C): 27.7%. Determination reuse is supported by public data (CLM-04); the other levers are modelled only.
disclosure: Modelled estimate, not measured at a customer.

claim: In Unbound's cost model, an advisor-distributed DAF provider running on Unbound spends about 36% less on administration than with its current workflow enhanced with AI: $375 per fund-year at the median (range $299–$480) against $589 (range $448–$786).
lever_attribution: Platform alone (B to C0): 10.2%. Redesign levers (C0 to C): 29.1%.
disclosure: Modelled estimate, not measured at a customer.

claim: In public Form 990 grant data for 20 DAF sponsors, about 1 in 9 recipients needed a person to confirm eligibility, but 64% of those had been granted to by the same sponsor the year before. By reusing earlier determinations, Unbound reduces first-time eligibility reviews to about 4% of recipients.
comparator: The same recipients without reuse (11.2% routed to a person)
conditions: Recipients receiving over $5,000 in a year; eligibility checks only (report 14 §5).
disclosure: Measured on public IRS data for recipients receiving over $5,000 a year; eligibility checks only.

claim: In Unbound's cost model, staff step in about half as often: 526 human interventions per 1,000 funds a year against 1,013 for a national sponsor's AI-enhanced current workflow (928 against 1,740 for an advisor-distributed provider).
disclosure: Modelled estimate, not measured at a customer.
